title: Retry Backoff Review
h1: Retry failed requests with exponential backoff
lede: Read the new retry helper first, then the client that uses it. Tick a file once you've reviewed it; ticks are saved in this browser.

summary: getJson retried three times back to back, and it treated HTTP errors as success. It now retries with exponential backoff and fails on any non-2xx response.
A new generic helper, withRetry, replaces retryThreeTimes. The client passes its attempts and base delay.
before: Three immediate retries, with no delay.
A 500 response was parsed as JSON and returned.
after: Three attempts, waiting 200 ms and then 400 ms between them.
A non-2xx response throws, so it's retried, and the last error is rethrown.

layout.role: Uses the helper and treats HTTP errors as failures.

decisions: Fixed exponential backoff without jitter, because there's only one caller today. (your call)

added.text: withRetry runs fn up to attempts times. It sleeps backoffDelay between attempts and rethrows the last error.

files.note: Generic helper with no HTTP knowledge.

lines.text: Delay doubles each attempt: 200, 400, 800 ms for a 200 ms base.
No sleep after the last attempt, so a failure surfaces right away.

tests.name: backoffDelay › doubles the delay on each attempt
tests.inputs: Attempts 0, 1 and 2 with a 100 ms base.
tests.why: Pins the backoff curve. withRetry itself has no test yet, which is a gap.

modified.text: getJson throws on non-2xx responses. Before, it parsed and returned error bodies.
Uses withRetry with 3 attempts and a 200 ms base delay.

files.note: The only caller of the retry helper.

lines.text: This is the user-visible fix: a 500 is now an error that gets retried.
